cohort: The study included a hospital-based cohort of 1185 pregnant women aged 16 years or older and their infants in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, between May 2020 and March 2022.
finding: SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy significantly increased the risk of adverse maternal outcomes, but no significant effect was observed on prematurity or other adverse perinatal outcomes, including fetal distress, stillbirth, and neonatal death.
mod_finding: Cesarean section deliveries were performed significantly more frequently in SARS-CoV-2 infected participants (57%) compared to uninfected participants (43%).
